chunk_findings.detail: `new = '[]'` is a TOML string, not the empty array `[]`. The knob `approvals.policy` is list-valued: it is meant to hold zero or more standing auto-approval policy IDs, so the default with no rules should be an empty list. When this fragment is consumed, the default becomes the string `"[]"`; code that iterates `approvals.policy` or assigns/validates it as a list will fail or behave incorrectly on the default configuration. Use `new = []`.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated extraction is not what landed. Intent requires the per-descriptor checks to live in this module and the existing suite (`tests/test_driver_conformance.py`) to call `run`. The change manifest only adds this new `run` and a CLI smoke test; the fixture-backed suite is untouched, so CLI conformance and the DRV-conformance tests are two copies that can disagree. A descriptor that fails `facts.problems` or has an unresolved `hookio` plan can still be green in one path and red in the other.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/driver_conformance.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only asserts `id="claude"` returns `status == "ok"`. A `run` that ignores the harness and always returns `{"agent": "claude", "status": "ok", "checks": {}}` satisfies it. Unknown fact status, `facts.problems`, a missing hook plan, and an unresolved normalizer/emitter — the only checks this module implements — are never given a failing input, so the test cannot show the wiring is wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: The new failing-path test added in `tests/test_driver_conformance.py` calls `DC.run` directly and monkeypatches `hookio.plan_for` to return `None`; it does not exercise the `ddflow harness test` CLI path. The CLI smoke test still only shows the happy path for `"claude"`: a `harness_drv.py` implementation that ignores the imported module and hardcodes `{"agent": "claude", "status": "ok", "checks": {}}` would still pass it. Unknown fact status, `facts.problems`, a missing hook plan, and unresolved normalizer/emitter remain untested through the actual CLI wiring, so the previous defect still holds.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_cli_drivers.py:test_test_runs_the_offline_conformance

chunk_findings.detail: The added success-path test still cannot detect a broken wiring: a `run` implementation in `ddflow.services.driver_conformance` that ignores the harness and always returns `{"agent": "claude", "status": "ok", "checks": {}}` passes it, because it only exercises `id="claude"` and asserts `status == "ok"` plus `agent == "claude"`. It never supplies a failing harness case (unknown fact status, `facts.problems`, missing hookio plan, unresolved normalizer/emitter), so the test remains vacuous for the offline conformance checks it claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_cli_drivers.py:test_test_runs_the_offline_conformance

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier vacuous-wiring finding still holds. `test_test_runs_the_offline_conformance` still only calls `harness_view(..., what="test", id="claude")` and asserts `result["status"] == "ok"`. A `run` that ignores its harness and always returns `{"agent": "claude", "status": "ok", "checks": {}}` still passes that test, so it does not show the CLI is bound to the real checks. The new `test_run_reports_failed_when_a_command_hooked_agent_has_no_plan` only calls `DC.run` after patching `hookio.plan_for`; it never goes through `harness_view`, and nothing feeds an unknown fact status, a `facts.problems` failure, or an unresolved normalizer/emitter. Those paths can be wrong in the module the CLI imports and both new tests stay green.

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor replaced the direct `harnessfacts.rows`/`facts.problems` assertions with `result = DC.run(h)` and asserts only `result["checks"]["facts"]["status"] == "ok"`. There is no corresponding failing-facts test, so a `DC.run` implementation that always reports `"facts": {"status": "ok"}` (or simply drops the `harnessfacts.rows` status check) still passes every `C.ALL` fixture. The extracted facts logic is therefore no longer independently guarded by this test; an input with an unknown fact status or a non-empty `facts.problems` would be needed to exercise the failed branch, and none is provided.
